$comment: Paragraphs that say the same thing twice, and which copy the reader meets second.
RULE 1b, IN FULL: a duplicate is COLLAPSED, not cut. Until Firefly approves deletion, the
second copy stays in the document and stays in the printed kit; it is folded behind a one-line
cross-reference naming the section that said it first. Nothing here removes a word.
WHICH SIDE IS THE DUPLICATE is a reading-order judgement, made here rather than by the detector,
which walks the chapters alphabetically. The duplicate is the copy the reader reaches SECOND in
lib/flow.ts's FLOW_ORDER — collapsing the first would point a reader forward at something they
have not read, which is worse than the repetition.
TWO OF THE THREE FLIPPED in the 2026 restructure. The ask moved from the front of the document
to the end of it, so the paragraphs it used to state first it now states last, and the copy in
§4.1 and §5.5 became the one the reader meets first.
